text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's weekly press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Botswana must take Singapore's development model seriously, especially the concept of productivity. Despite the exhortations of President Ketumile Masire, productivity seems not to have taken root in Botswana. A Singaporean trade delegation visited Botswana this week.

- Workers at Debswana's three diamond mines are dissatisfied with a package offered to workers who will be laid off after the recent introduction of continuous operations and the Botswana Mineworkers' Union is to make a submission to the Commissioner of Labour. There have been demonstrations, but no work stoppages, which are illegal in Botswana. Debswana is a 50/50 joint venture between De Beers and the government.

- The Botswana pula should be delinked from the South African rand, as it is turning away potential investors and hitting local manufacturers. The policy was meant to protect their exports, but they now have to pay more for imported raw materials.
- Members of a visiting Singaporean trade delegation expressed concern over the pula-rand link.
- Preparations are going ahead for a Southern Africa Development Community cultural festival in Namibia starting on August 25.
